subject: Climate & Environment
title: Mangrove Forests
description: A quick, practical guide to Mangrove Forests.

hook.text: Mangroves grow where land meets sea — roots tangled in saltwater, defying the tides.

buildup.text: They protect coastlines from storms, filter water, and serve as nurseries for fish.

discovery.text: Mangroves store up to 4 times more carbon per hectare than tropical rainforests.

twist.text: Half the world's mangroves have been destroyed for shrimp farms and coastal development.

climax.text: Losing mangroves exposes coasts to flooding and releases massive stores of buried carbon.

punchline.text: The trees standing in the ocean are worth more than the land behind them.

quiz.question: How do mangroves compare to rainforests in carbon storage per hectare?
options: They store up to 4 times more

details.summary: Mangrove forests grow in coastal saltwater environments across the tropics, protecting shorelines from storms, serving as nurseries for marine life, and storing up to five times more carbon per hectare than terrestrial forests. Over a third have been lost since the 1980s.
details.whyItMatters: Mangroves deliver outsized benefits per hectare for climate, fisheries, and disaster protection. Their rapid loss is one of the most cost-effective conservation crises to address.
takeaways: Mangroves store carbon in dense root systems and anaerobic soil
They reduce wave energy by up to 66 percent, protecting coastlines
Shrimp farming and coastal development are the main destruction drivers

faq.question: How do mangroves protect against storms and tsunamis?
faq.answer: Dense root networks and canopy absorb wave energy and slow storm surges. Communities behind mangrove belts suffer significantly less flooding and property damage during hurricanes and cyclones compared to exposed coastlines.

faq.question: Why are mangroves being destroyed?
faq.answer: Shrimp and fish ponds, coastal development, agriculture, and pollution have destroyed over a third of mangrove area since the 1980s. Restoration is possible but takes decades because mangrove ecosystems are complex and sensitive to water conditions.
